cross_package_notes.note: Verified #128 cross-unit storageurl tenant scoping note in internal/im/service.go:216: newOutboundFileServiceResolver resolves storage backends strictly from the owning tenant (req.tenant.ID) and authorized shared-agent/KB resource catalogs via resolveResourceStorageForTenant, rejecting disabled/deleted or cross-tenant unshared backends before presigning or rewriting APP_EXTERNAL_URL links.

Verified read-only schema parity with im_channel_sessions partial unique indexes idx_channel_lookup (platform, user_id, chat_id, tenant_id, agent_id) and idx_channel_thread_lookup (platform, chat_id, thread_id, tenant_id, agent_id): resolveUserSession and resolveThreadSession predicate every lookup and insert on channel.TenantID + channel.AgentID + platform, checkDuplicateBot prevents cross-tenant duplicate bot registration, and sessionService.GetSession executes under tenant-scoped sessionCtx.

Verified read-only HTTP handler callers propagate authenticated c.Request.Context() (carrying types.TenantIDContextKey) into QRCodeService.GetLoginQRCode and PollQRCodeStatus and run VerifyCallback prior to HandleURLVerification and ParseCallback on every IM webhook route.

invariants_checked: IMChannel.computeBotIdentity hashes secret webhook tokens (Mattermost outgoing_token, Yunzhijia yzjtoken, and malformed colon-less Telegram bot_token fallbacks) with SHA-256 so IMChannelSummary responses and plaintext bot_identity DB columns never expose raw credentials, while SYSTEM_AES_KEY AES-256-GCM encrypts stored channel credentials.

HandleMessage deduplication keys are scoped by channelID + messageID across both Redis SetNX (genyee:im:dedup:*, fail-closed on Redis errors) and single-instance sync.Map caches, preventing cross-tenant/cross-channel message ID collisions, and dynamic DB fallback refuses to start disabled channels.

Multi-tenant session routing (resolveUserSession, resolveThreadSession), per-user sliding-window rate limiting (genyee:im:ratelimit:*), bounded QA worker queues, distributed leader election (Lua-fenced genyee:im:leader:*), inbound webhook/attachment size caps (LimitWebhookBody 1 MiB, ReadIMResponse 10 MiB, ReadIMAttachmentResponse 100 MiB), outbound storageurl tenant scoping (#128), and /info + /search KBSelectionMode enforcement all uphold tenant and agent isolation with zero legacy brand residues.

findings.summary: IMChannel.computeBotIdentity stored raw Mattermost outgoing_token secrets ("mattermost:wh:" + tok) and colon-less Telegram bot_token fallbacks in plaintext bot_identity, leaking webhook credentials through IMChannelSummary list APIs and unencrypted DB columns.

HandleMessage keyed message deduplication on unscoped msg.MessageID across all channels/tenants (allowing sequential or colliding platform-local message IDs to drop another tenant's messages for 5 minutes) and dynamically started disabled DB channels when absent from the active adapter map.

InfoCommand listed stale Config.KnowledgeBases names even when KBSelectionMode was "none", SearchCommand invoked SearchKnowledge with empty kbIDs when KBs were disabled/unconfigured, and both commands lacked nil-service/context guards.

invariants_checked: VerifyCallback enforces non-empty clientSecret, mandatory timestamp and sign headers, 1-hour millisecond replay window, and constant-time HMAC-SHA256 verification before callback parsing.

Temporary file download URLs and session_webhook reply URLs enforce HTTPS without userinfo on strict DingTalk/Aliyun OSS host suffixes backed by SSRFSafeHTTPClient dial-time IP validation and bounded response readers.
OpenAPI replies honor configured apiBaseURL for both direct and group chats, and FinalizeStream surfaces card streaming errors so Service triggers its plain-text SendReply fallback.

findings.summary: defaultValidateFileDownloadURL and isAllowedDingTalkDownloadHost matched .aliyuncs.com and .dingtalk.com host suffixes without requiring https scheme, rejecting URL userinfo, or rejecting bare suffix hostnames, bypassing ValidateURLForSSRF on non-HTTPS or credential-bearing URLs.

replyViaOpenAPI hardcoded https://api.dingtalk.com instead of configured apiBaseURL, and FinalizeStream swallowed streamingUpdateCard failures instead of returning an error for plain-text fallback delivery.

invariants_checked: VerifyCallback fails closed when verificationToken is empty, validates X-Lark-Request-Timestamp (5-minute skew) and X-Lark-Signature (constant-time SHA-256) prior to AES-CBC decryption whenever present, and requires both headers on all encrypted non-url_verification events.
Adapter.decrypt enforces minimum 2-block length and 16-byte AES block alignment prior to cipher.CBCDecrypter.CryptBlocks and validates PKCS#7 padding in constant time across the final block.
Feishu/Lark regional endpoints, SSRFSafeHTTPClient media downloads, Content-Disposition RFC 5987 filename decoding, WebSocket long-connection lifecycle, and stream reaper cleanup operate race-free.

findings.summary: Adapter.decrypt invoked cipher.CBCDecrypter.CryptBlocks after stripping the 16-byte IV without checking block alignment or non-empty ciphertext, allowing an unauthenticated webhook request with non-block-aligned base64 ciphertext to panic the server before X-Lark-Signature was checked.

invariants_checked: VerifyCallback fails closed immediately when outgoingToken is empty before reading or parsing the request body, enforces LimitWebhookBody (1 MiB) and bounded form key/parameter counts, and compares outgoing tokens with subtle.ConstantTimeCompare.

Mattermost REST v4 client validates server URLs via ValidateURLForSSRF + SSRFSafeHTTPClient, validates postID and fileID path segments against traversal/query/fragment injection before authenticated Bearer requests, and truncates error previews on valid UTF-8 rune boundaries.

findings.summary: GetPost, PatchPostMessage, GetFileInfo, and GetFileReader interpolated webhook-supplied postID and fileID values directly into authenticated REST v4 URL paths without path-segment validation (enabling ../ traversal onto arbitrary Mattermost API routes), and VerifyCallback parsed untrusted bodies before checking empty outgoingToken.

invariants_checked: Webhook callback verification derives the Ed25519 key deterministically from non-empty appSecret, enforces 5-minute X-Signature-Timestamp skew and hex signature decoding, and signs url-verification responses only after Ed25519 verification.
REST and WebSocket clients enforce SSRF validation on api_base_url and wss:// gateway_url, resolve /gateway against configured apiBaseURL, and validate C2C/group OpenIDs before path construction.

LongConnClient synchronizes sequence numbers under c.mu, serializes WebSocket JSON writes under c.writeMu, bounds frame sizes (1 MiB), guards DialContext/Stop races, and cancels per-connection heartbeat goroutines cleanly on reconnect or shutdown.

findings.summary: LongConnClient mutated and shared c.seq without locking while heartbeatLoop marshaled it concurrently (data race), wrote concurrently to ws.Conn without a write mutex, leaked heartbeat goroutines across reconnects, and raced Stop() with DialContext; Client.GatewayURL also hardcoded defaultGatewayURL instead of c.apiBaseURL and omitted path-segment validation on openID/groupOpenID.

invariants_checked: VerifyCallback fails closed when signingSecret is empty, caps inbound webhook bodies via LimitWebhookBody, and verifies Slack HMAC-SHA256 signatures and 5-minute replay timestamps via slack.NewSecretsVerifier.
DownloadFile strictly restricts Bearer-authenticated file downloads to https://files.slack.com and https://slack.com/files-pri/ on default port 443 without userinfo via SSRFSafeHTTPClient.

Socket Mode factory requires non-empty app_token and bot_token before starting background workers, LongConnClient guards closed Events channels and nil evt.Request pointers, and FinalizeStream surfaces chat.update errors for fallback delivery.

findings.summary: LongConnClient.Start panicked on EventsAPI events with nil evt.Request and busy-spun if client.Events closed before ctx cancellation; NewFactory spawned Socket Mode goroutines with empty app_token/bot_token; and FinalizeStream swallowed UpdateMessageContext errors.

invariants_checked: VerifyCallback fails closed when secretToken or X-Telegram-Bot-Api-Secret-Token is empty and compares tokens with subtle.ConstantTimeCompare.

All Bot API and file download transport errors redact embedded bot<token> URL credentials while preserving error unwrapping (errors.Is/As), DownloadFile validates getFile file_path against traversal/query/fragment injection, FinalizeStream surfaces terminal edit failures, and websocket mode rejects empty bot_token.

findings.summary: Telegram HTTP transport errors wrapped *url.Error values containing cleartext /bot<bot_token>/ URLs into logs and caller errors; DownloadFile interpolated unvalidated getFile file_path into /file/bot<token>/<file_path>; FinalizeStream swallowed plain-text retry errors; and websocket factory accepted empty bot_token.

invariants_checked: Personal WeChat iLink bot channel preserved and hardened: AES-128-ECB PKCS#7 media encryption/decryption validates key length (16 bytes), block alignment, and constant-bounds padding, and bounds encrypted media downloads via ReadIMAttachmentResponse (100 MiB).

QRCodeService binds issued login QR tokens to the requesting tenant (types.TenantIDFromContext) with 10-minute TTL eviction so cross-tenant PollQRCodeStatus calls cannot hijack pending bot_token credentials, cancels upstream long-polls on client disconnect (context.Canceled), and never echoes raw response bodies in errors.
LongPollClient bounds concurrent message-handler goroutines with a semaphore and waits for in-flight handlers via sync.WaitGroup before Start returns on channel stop or token expiry.

findings.summary: Singleton QRCodeService allowed cross-tenant PollQRCodeStatus polling of another tenant's login qrcode token, leaked raw response bodies (potentially containing bot_token) on JSON decode errors, and ignored client disconnects; LongPollClient spawned unbounded detached message-handler goroutines without waiting on channel stop.

invariants_checked: Enterprise WeCom bot channel preserved and hardened across both webhook and aibot WebSocket modes: VerifyCallback fails closed on empty token, enforces 5-minute timestamp skew, caps XML body reads via LimitWebhookBody, and checks SHA-1 signatures with subtle.ConstantTimeCompare.

WebhookAdapter validates 32-byte decoded EncodingAESKey at construction, verifies 32-byte PKCS#7 padding and corp_id in constant time without leaking expected corp_id, guards 20+msgLen against uint32 overflow slice panics, URL-escapes query credentials, and redacts access_token/corpsecret from transport errors.

WSAdapter bounds encrypted media downloads via ReadIMAttachmentResponse (100 MiB) instead of unbounded io.ReadAll, strips full 1..32-byte WeCom PKCS#7 padding in decryptAESCBC, enforces HTTPS without userinfo in isAllowedIMAPIHost, and sets a 4 MiB WebSocket frame read limit.

findings.summary: WebhookAdapter.decrypt checked uint32(len(plaintext)) < 20+msgLen, allowing crafted msgLen >= 0xFFFFFFEC to wrap uint32 addition to 0..19 and panic with slice bounds out of range [20:0]; it also leaked expected corpID on mismatch and accepted wrong-length EncodingAESKey at construction.

WSAdapter.DownloadFile read encrypted media via unbounded io.ReadAll(reader) (enabling OOM) and rejected valid 17..32-byte WeCom PKCS#7 padding in decryptAESCBC; isAllowedIMAPIHost accepted non-HTTPS/userinfo URLs; and query tokens lacked URL escaping and error redaction.

invariants_checked: VerifyCallback fails closed when appSecret or sign header is empty, enforces 5-minute millisecond timestamp replay window, caps body reads via LimitWebhookBody, and verifies canonical HMAC-SHA1 signatures in constant time.

SendReply, WebSocket URLs, and attachment downloads enforce HTTPS/WSS without userinfo, strict host suffix allowlisting, SSRF_DNS_WHITELIST_ONLY compliance, single-redirect off-host Authorization stripping, and 20 MiB download caps.

HTTP and WebSocket dial errors scrub yzjtoken query secrets while preserving error unwrapping, and LongConnClient checks closed state under c.mu immediately after DialContext so concurrent Stop() never blocks on ReadMessage.

findings.summary: Adapter.SendReply and LongConnClient.connectAndRun surfaced *url.Error strings containing cleartext ?yzjtoken=<secret> query credentials into logs and caller errors, and connectAndRun assigned c.conn without re-checking c.closed under c.mu after DialContext (causing Stop() races to block for the 45s read timeout).
